US-33 · Designer portal14 October 2026For Kody and the founding partners

Why the portal feels slow, and what to fix first

The ask: the portal has started to feel sluggish. Page loads should show a loading indicator or skeletons, a click should make something happen at once, and engineers and designers together should find the code and infrastructure changes that remove the wait. This document is the team's answer. Nothing in the product changed to write it.

A hard load spends about seven seconds in a fixed queue before the studio sees its work, and no screen says anything is happening while it waits. The two largest causes are a queue of sixteen user lookups, about 2.7 s, and the script weight, about 3 s. The first goes with one small change; the second only shrinks.

The top five moves all in Fix now · no ruling needed · no flag

  1. Read the signed-in user once, from the session. Sixteen auth/v1/user calls run one after another, about 172 ms each, and every data read waits behind them.−2.7 s per hard loadF1 · review/e2-page-architecture.md §0 · synthesis/pairings.md M11 · about −4.2 s on a Document
  2. Stop shipping every icon and the crypto polyfill to every page. Three chunks ride on every route, sign-in included.−220 to −390 KB gzipF8, F9, F10 · review/e3-infra-bundle.md §4e · baseline/bundle.md
  3. Let the browser keep the hashed scripts. Every hard load asks the server again about all 63 scripts.63 → 0 revalidationsF7 · baseline/BASELINE.md:99-102 · prod walk
  4. When a task is ticked, refresh only what the tick changed. Today one tick reloads the whole Desk as well.27 → 3 refetches per tickF5 · baseline/data/e1-P6-1440.json · review/e1-data-writes.md §1.1
  5. Answer every press, and never show a blank room. A press state on every act, 44 px task rows, and shaped placeholders in the rooms that draw nothing today.B1 met at the press · no blank roomF13, F16 · baseline/BASELINE.md:52-53 · screens/P4-200ms.jpg

Said plainly

The proposed budget B3, usable content within 1.5 s, cannot hold on a cold hard load in the lab on any track. After every track, about 1.2 MB of JavaScript still crosses a link of about 1 MB/s and is parsed at 4× CPU slowdown. A hard load lands at 2.6–3.6 s at best EST. Clicks inside the portal can meet 1.5 s, and most already do. PQ1 therefore asks to split B3 into B3a for navigation (≤1.5 s) and B3b for hard loads (≤3.5 s).

synthesis/plan.md §2 "Estimates" and PQ1

Loading direction, recommended: Q, Quiet paper, with arrival option C, where the placeholder becomes the arrival instead of hiding the finished page. Action feedback, recommended: one quiet grammar. Something answers within 100 ms, a word appears only when a write is slow, and nothing ever claims a send, a payment or a delete before the server confirms it.

2 Baseline

What "sluggish" is, measured

The baseline seat timed ten scenarios, P1 to P10, in a throttled local lab: a production build, local Supabase, Chromium at 4× CPU slowdown on a Fast 4G profile, three cold runs each, at 1440 and 390 wide. A read-only signed-in walk on app.patina.cloud added prod network timings. E1 later measured the task tick (P6) on the same lab. Every figure below names its file.

Local data is thin: 16 projects for Leah's local studio, not 43. Prod's heavier documents will be equal or slower. The prod tab was hidden, so prod paint timings are missing; prod numbers are network and server timings. baseline/BASELINE.md "Caveats"

3 Findings

Findings by discipline

Five seats read the code and the baseline on their own, then a lead reconciled them. Each finding below names where it was seen. Paths are relative to apps/designer-portal/src/ unless they start with packages/; data files are under baseline/.

Loading D1 · review/d1-loading.md

  1. L1

    The studio waits in three silences. Dead air after a click: 215–251 ms locally and 248–608 ms in prod with nothing on screen changing. Blank paper on a hard load: first paint at about 0.7 s, usable at about 7 s. And rooms that draw nothing at all.BASELINE.md:49-60, 89-96 · P1hard 6,974 ms, P2hard 6,773 ms · d1 §0

  2. L2

    Five loading treatments, plus a hidden sixth. About 20 different prose lines ("Picking up…", "Reading the roster…"), StrataSweep, SectionLoadingLine, two real skeletons, and nothing. The arrival veil is the sixth: the page is laid out, then hidden on purpose, for up to 1.5 s on the Desk and 8.5 s on a held Document.d1 §1 · lib/arrival/arrival.css:8,15,23 · doc/[id]/page.tsx:3013-3021

  3. L3

    Loading that looks empty. The Desk's frames are hollow outlines and the recent-boards tiles are white cards with a border. At one second the Desk looks like three empty boards.desk/page.tsx:581-606 · recent-boards-strip.tsx:102 · screens/P1-1000ms.jpg

  4. L4

    Two rooms are blank, and People reads "empty" while it loads. The build room renders fallback={null} and Room view returns null while loading. "Reading the roster…" has no role="status" or aria-busy, so screen readers never hear it.doc/[id]/pieces/page.tsx:51 · rooms/room-view/room-view.tsx:279 · people/views/directory-view.tsx:571 · BASELINE.md:52-53

  5. L5

    On the Document the arrival hides finished work; on the Desk it hides almost nothing. A Document hard load is usable at 6,773 ms but its largest paint comes at 10,728 ms, because the held paper waits for the Desk enrichment. On the Desk the first data read only starts at 5,951 ms. Retiring the arrival alone would not make the Desk fast.BASELINE.md:50 · pairings.md M14 · e2 §0, §3.4

Action feedback D2 · review/d2-feedback.md

  1. A1

    A tick changes nothing for 465–748 ms. That misses B1 by 4.6 to 7.5 times. The tick is a plain button with a hover style and no press state; the work-block row is about 29 px tall and the coordination tick 13 px, both under the 44 px rule.e1-P6-1440.json · work-block.tsx:312-317 · coordination-work.tsx:177-178

  2. A2

    Failures land far from the act. A failed tick shows the raw database message in a red toast in the corner. Adding a room closes the form at once and loses the typed name if the write fails.lib/error-handler.ts:811-820 · ffe-section.tsx:934-946 · d2 §4

  3. A3

    Two deletes already pretend. Removing a folio image and deleting a palette swatch update the screen before the server agrees, with no Undo. Under the honesty rule they become pending-only until Undo exists (PQ14).piece-folio.tsx:96 · palette-swatch-editor.tsx:61-73

  4. A4

    Every write retries once on a network error, sends and money included. An ambiguous failure on a send could send twice. Fix now turns retry off for send and money hooks unless they carry an idempotency key.lib/react-query.ts:242-249 · plan F15 · open check O4

  5. A5

    Most of the grammar exists already. "Completing…" and "Sending" hold at the press, and the Desk has a press style. The work is to make every act use them.phase-advance-control.tsx:324-347 · globals.css:943-955 · d2 §1

Data & writes E1 · review/e1-data-writes.md

  1. D1

    The Desk's read runs on every Document. The command bar loads the Desk unconditionally, and it is mounted for every Document route. That read is 24 requests plus one RPC per live purchase order, and it polls every 60 s.components/document/command-bar.tsx:404 · app/(document)/layout.tsx:125 · hooks/use-desk-engagements.ts:486-492, 690-739

  2. D2

    One tick causes 27 refetches, and 24 of them are the Desk. The new state shows at 748 ms; the network settles at 1,368 ms. After the tick's own refetch, the remaining 650–700 ms is all Desk traffic.baseline/data/e1-P6-1440.json · e1 §1.1

  3. D3

    Invalidation is broad by habit. 51 single-line invalidations of the whole ['document-state'] key across 38 files, 1,400 invalidateQueries lines, and 9 optimistic sites in 7 files.e1 §0.5

  4. D4

    The user lookup is a lock, not just a call. The installed auth library runs getUser()'s network call inside its client lock, and every data request takes the same lock for its token. So 212 hook-level lookups become a queue that every read waits behind.@supabase/auth-js@2.98.0 GoTrueClient.js:1258-1265 · supabase-js index.mjs:329-335 · pairings.md M11

  5. D5

    The Desk can show a sent draft as ready to send for up to a minute. Sending or discarding a draft does not mark the Desk stale.packages/supabase/src/hooks/use-outbound-drafts.ts:47,59,67 · use-desk-engagements.ts:692,707

Page architecture E2 · review/e2-page-architecture.md

  1. P1

    Where a Desk hard load's 6.9 s goes. Scripts until 3,016 ms; sixteen user lookups back to back from 3,258 to 6,485 ms; the first data read at 5,951 ms, after 15 of the 16; content at 6,926 ms.baseline/traces/local-desk-waterfall.json · e2 §0

  4. P4

    The Desk reads itself twice on /desk. Two query keys for the same data, one with the studio id in it: about 48 extra requests per hard load.desk/page.tsx:131 · hooks/use-desk-engagements.ts:1071 · e2 §3.1

  1. B1

What we expected, and what we found

The plan's code sweep went in with hypotheses. These are the ones the evidence turned over.

ExpectedA realtime echo and a double subscription make each write refetch twice.
Found · RJ5Neither exists today. The three coordination tables are not in the realtime publication locally, the lab saw 0 change frames after a write, and the band that subscribed a second time is no longer mounted. The hazard is latent; prod membership is unverified (O1).e1 §0.3-0.4 · e1-P6-1440.json realtimeEchoFrames
ExpectedRebuilding the design system with code splitting would shrink the bundle.
Found · RJ1It changes nothing here: the portal compiles the design system from source. The leak is the client boundary in the root layout and the icon lookup (F9, F10).tsconfig.json:25 · e3 §4b
ExpectedA 790 KB chunk was a MIME table with no source.
FoundIt is mostly lucide icons (449 KB of 768 KB parsed). The MIME table is 26 KB.BASELINE.md:175 · bundle.md:41
ExpectedThe arrival hold is the seven seconds.
FoundThe seven seconds are scripts, the user-lookup queue and the reads. The hold costs 2–4 s on a Document and almost nothing on the Desk.pairings.md M14
ExpectedThe Library is blank while it loads, and the Desk ships about 1.37 MB.
FoundThe Library shows a placeholder at 647 ms. The Desk ships more than expected: 1,586 KB.BASELINE.md:157, 172
ExpectedExcluding public/three from middleware would save time.
Found · RJ2Static assets never reach the Worker in prod, so it saves nothing.e3 §1e

4 Proposals

Paired proposals, engineering × design

Every design proposal was paired with the engineering change that makes it possible, and every engineering change with what a studio member would feel. Where the seats disagreed, the lead ruled and recorded why. The full map is synthesis/pairings.md; the ids below run through the tracks in §5.

"Would feel" lines are the seats' projections. No studio member was asked, and none is quoted.

F1 · N1 · E1-9
Engineering

A session-user store seeded once from the session, replacing hook-level user lookups.

Design

None needed. It removes the wait the placeholders would otherwise have to cover.

Would feel

Every hard load about 2.7 s shorter. The largest single change.

F13 · N10 · D1.1–D1.7 · E2-1
Engineering

One skeleton component per room, rendered at three mount points with identical geometry.

Design

One loading register: real frame, pearl placeholders in the real line boxes, an indicator, and words only when slow.

Would feel

No room is ever blank. People stops looking empty while it loads.

N10 · PQ3 · D1.12 · E2-6
Engineering

Remove the held-paper path; seed the job title from the Desk cache on intent.

Design

Arrival option C: the placeholder becomes the arrival, with the job's name set at first paint.

Would feel

The Document's finished paper is no longer hidden for 2–4 s.

F5 → N3 · D2.3 · E1-2, E1-3
Engineering

Narrow the tick's invalidation first, then an optimistic helper with snapshot and restore.

Design

The tick lands under the finger; "saving…" only past 400 ms; a failure restores the truth inline.

Would feel

The tick answers at once instead of after about three quarters of a second.

F16 · D2.2, D2.18, D2.19
Engineering

Press states, aria-pressed, aria-busy, and 44 px task rows.

Design

S0: every act answers the press, rows included.

Would feel

No click goes unacknowledged.

N11 · PQ4 · D1.9
Engineering

A capture-phase link listener and a wrapped router.push start the rule; no busy region ends it.

Design

A 1 px ink rule at the top of the paper, from 300 ms.

Would feel

Something speaks on a slow navigation, and nothing flashes on a fast one.

N7 · PQ18 · E1-4, E2-5
Engineering

The command bar reads the Desk only when open; the Document reads a scoped "this job's needs".

Design

None needed.

Would feel

The Document stops "finishing" seconds after it looks ready. EST −0.5 to −1.5 s.

F6 · F15 · N12 · D2.12, D2.13
Engineering

Mark the Desk stale after a send; no automatic retry on send and money hooks.

Design

Sends stay pending-only: "Sending", then "Still sending." at 8 s; never "sent" before the receipt.

Would feel

A sent draft stops reading as ready to send; nothing is sent twice by a retry.

The two loading directions, side by side

Both directions share the same structure and meet B2 equally, because the timing comes from the engineering mount points, not the material. They differ in voice. Q builds from what the paper already uses: pearl bars that breathe slowly and a hairline rule. X adds shimmer, a glowing bar and toasts. The team recommends Q (PQ2), because the studio promise is that the studio won't notice Patina.

Q · Quiet paper recommended

A Document at about 200 ms, 390 wide. The job title is set at first paint (arrival C).

X · Expressive

The same moment, with shimmer and the glow bar.

The strongest argument against Q. Kody asked for "a loading indicator or skeletons", and a 1 px rule at 40% ink may not register as an indicator at all. Branaghan and Sanchez (2009) found people prefer more feedback, and no first-party source shows calm tools deliberately leaving progress out. Q's quietness is a taste call, not evidence. If a studio walk shows the rule goes unnoticed, the fallback inside Q is a 2 px rule at 60%, still without X's bar and toasts.synthesis/plan.md §4 · review/r-patterns.md §1-2 · pairings.md R-5, R-6

Both directions on the Document at 1440
At four seconds: Q's slow line and X's toast

Rooms with no arrival get placeholders now

The build room and People draw nothing while they load today. Their placeholders ship in Fix now (F13) as still pearl bars, with no ruling needed. The breath and the rule wait for PQ2 and PQ5.

The navigation rule

A click on a link or a router.push starts it; the new page having no busy region ends it. It appears only after 300 ms, so warm navigations show nothing and a slow one does. On failure it stops and an inline line takes over. Press the live frame to play it.

The rule at start, and on failure, at 1440

Action feedback: one grammar for every click

Within 100 ms exactly one thing answers the click. What answers depends on whether the act may show its result before the server confirms it.

StageWhenInternal acts (optimistic)Sends, money, server-decided acts (pending-only)
S0 press0 msA press state; the row warmsSame
S1 answer≤100 msThe value changes (a sage tick; a faint ghost row for creates)The verb changes ("Completing…", "Sending"), held, aria-busy, guarded against a second press
S2 pendingafter 400 ms, held ≥500 mssaving… in the row's meta columnAlready showing; "Still working." at 8 s
S3 settledon the write's own responseThe meta returns to the server's truth; nothing celebratesA receipt in plain words
S4 failureon errorRestore the truth; one role="alert" line; a 44 px Try again; keep the typed wordsThe word returns, and says what is true now ("Nothing was sent.")
S5 Undoonly where a restore path existsAn in-flow Undo row takes focusNever

Never optimistic

External sends (drafts, invoices, plan issues, transmittals, trade texts). Money (payments, invoice lines, PO release, timer stop). Deletes without Undo. Outcomes the server decides (phase advance, placing a piece, promotion to the studio library, holds, archive). And any word that claims an outside fact before the receipt: "sent", "paid", "removed", "approved by client". Never, in either direction: confetti, checkmark bursts, counters that count up, streaks, "nice work", or sound.synthesis/plan.md §5.2 · BRIEF.md "Honesty"

Each strip below has a scrubber. Pick a server time and an outcome, then play it; the column for the current stage lights.

Where the seats disagreed

IdThe disagreementRuling
M1Design wants an instant tick, but each write fans out to 27 refetches, and the settle rules differed between E1 and D2.Narrowing (F5) ships before the optimistic tick (N3). Optimistic acts end their pending state at the write; the refetch reconciles in the background.
M3A loading.tsx placeholder and today's arrival would show three waiting faces in a row on the Document.Desk and Document placeholders wait for the arrival ruling (PQ3); rooms without an arrival get theirs now (F13).
M5E2 would drive the rule from useLinkStatus; R found it skips prefetched links.D1's capture-phase signal instead (RJ16).
M6D1 started the indicator at 100 ms; R's sources say no indicator under about 1 s, and Turbo waits 500 ms.300 ms. The press state already covers B1. Ratified through PQ8.
M8E2 would slow polls while realtime is subscribed; E1 showed the channel can be subscribed and receive nothing.Rejected until the publication is checked (RJ6, O1).
M10E1: getClaims falls back to a network call for HS256 tokens. E3: Strata signs ES256.Both hold, for different callers. Middleware verifies with getClaims and an inlined key set (N13); browser hooks use the session store (F1). One live token header confirms the algorithm (O2).
M11Why do sixteen user lookups run one at a time?The auth library holds a client lock across the network call, and every read waits on the same lock. This made F1 the largest lever.
M14Is the arrival hold the seven seconds?No. On the Desk it hides almost nothing; on the Document it hides 2–4 s. PQ3 is about honesty and continuity as much as speed.

5 Tracks

Three tracks

Fix now items each take about a day or less, need no ruling and ship without a flag. Next items need a ruling, a flag or a few days. Structural items are multi-slice or wait on a measurement. Effort: S is a day or less, M several days, L several slices. Every gate reruns baseline/harness/lab.mjs under the same throttling unless it says otherwise.

Order inside Fix now: F17 first, so every other gate has a baseline. Then F1 and F7–F10, the largest gains. F5 lands before N3. F13 and F16 can run alongside everything.

7 Rulings

Founder questions

Each departure from the design canon, and each product or access decision a proposal needs, is a question here with the team's recommendation. Fix now waits on none of them. Four gate the Next track and are marked to decide first: PQ1 sets the bar every gate measures against, PQ2 and PQ3 gate the loading register (N10), and PQ9 gates optimistic ink (N3). PQ10 sets how both flags roll out.

  1. PQ1

    Ratify B1–B4, with B3 split into B3a (navigation ≤1.5 s p75) and B3b (hard load ≤3.5 s p75, lab and RUM)? Read B2 on a hard load as "at first paint", and watch cold Worker TTFB p75 in RUM.

    Touches: the contract budgets

    RecommendYes. B3 at 1.5 s cannot hold on a cold hard load under the lab's network on any track.

  2. PQ2

    Loading direction: Q, X, or a hybrid?

    Touches: the paper canon, ink-word state

    RecommendQ, Quiet paper.

  3. PQ3

    The arrival: A keep, B shorten, C the placeholder becomes the arrival, or D retire?

    Touches: V12, arrival v3 and its patch-1 hold caps

    RecommendC. A keeps 2–4 s of hidden paper on the Document; B rarely plays; D loses US-14 for nothing C does not give.

  4. PQ4

    May a navigation indicator exist, as Q's ink rule at the top of the paper?

    Touches: "Nothing on the Desk ever moves" (globals.css:305-306)

    RecommendYes, from 300 ms.

  5. PQ5

    May placeholders breathe on R15, beyond the spine marker?

    Touches: R15

    RecommendYes. A still bar on a 4 s wait reads as frozen. Reduced motion stills it.

  6. PQ6

    Demote StrataSweep to work of unknown shape only?

    Touches: R35

    RecommendYes.

  7. PQ7

    Retire the ~20 prose loading lines, keeping words only for slow, stalled and failed?

    Touches: the house loading voice

    RecommendYes.

  8. PQ8

    Thresholds: placeholders 150 ms, rule 300 ms, pending word 400 ms held ≥500 ms, slow 4 s, still working 8 s, stall 10 s?

    Touches: new values

    RecommendAs listed. Each is design practice, not research.

  9. PQ9

    Optimistic ink for internal toggles, edits, creates and reorder, with the never-optimistic list held?

    Touches: ink shows intent before the server confirms

    RecommendYes.

  10. PQ10

    Flag strategy?

    Touches: rollout

    RecommendFix now ships unflagged. Two PostHog flags: optimistic-ink (N3–N5, N15) and loading-register (N10, N11). Each is verified before enabling, rolled to Leah's studio by user id first, then to everyone after a week with no rise in failed writes or arrival declines. Never targeted by email.

  11. PQ11

    Retire the red global "Error" toast for Document writes, giving every act an inline line?

    Touches: extends R83

    RecommendYes.

  12. PQ12

    One band-level saving… that disappears, rather than "Saved · 10:42"?

    Touches: new chrome

    RecommendThe quiet one.

  13. PQ13

    The expressive extras: shimmer, glow, toasts, hairline, settle wash, a fixed Undo row with a shadow?

    Touches: D4 no shadows, R15, ink-word state

    RecommendNo, unless PQ2 picks X.

  14. PQ14

    Undo for folio image remove and swatch delete, instead of a browser confirm?

    Touches: new Undo surfaces

    RecommendYes.

  15. PQ15

    Offline: ticks and edits wait and save on reconnect; sends and money refuse with "You're offline. Nothing was sent."

    Touches: new band copy

    RecommendYes, after O3 confirms the pause behaviour.

  16. PQ16

    The 8 s send line: "Still sending." always; "Nothing is sent twice." only if the send is proven idempotent?

    Touches: new copy

    RecommendYes, conditional on O4.

  17. PQ17

    Publish the coordination tables to realtime?

    Touches: product behaviour; WAL and RLS cost per subscriber

    RecommendNot now. The 30 s polls are honest. Revisit after O1, and only with S7's registry.

  18. PQ18

    The Document reads a scoped "this job's needs" instead of the whole Desk?

    Touches: the letterhead's source

    RecommendYes (N7).

  19. PQ19

    Authorise three read-only prod checks: the publication list (O1), one token header and the JWT expiry (O2), and p95 list sizes (O9)?

    Touches: prod access is read-only and walk-only today

    RecommendYes, as read-only SQL with no client data.

  20. PQ20

    A Custom Access Token Hook carrying the designer role, run on every app's sign-in?

    Touches: auth blast radius

    RecommendDefer. After N13 the role query costs about 30 ms. Revisit only if RUM shows middleware matters.

Not a question: 44 px task rows. The 44 px rule is not waivable, so F16 ships it; the only effect is taller work blocks. synthesis/plan.md §6
